text:
Sophie: Quick heads-up — initial bring-up of the new reranker 'rk-2-large' with int8 quant shows a ~0.013 absolute drop in NDCG@10 vs float32 on our primary holdout. Anyone else seeing similar?

David: Same here on my sweep. MRR also down for short queries. Not sure if it’s quant noise or something in the eval harness. @Chen did you change any truncation defaults recently?

Chen: I didn’t change truncation, but I did push a small tokenizer tweak last week. I ran a small repro: float32 vs int8 on the same export, same seeds. The gap shows up only when we use sliding-context concatenation (query + doc-window) vs doc-first full-context. My hunch: tokenization boundary + prefix trimming interacts with KV cache offsets under int8.

Priya: FYI our eval harness currently pads to max_seq and then slices windows, which can move doc boundaries by a token or two. For short queries that can flip candidate order when scores tie. That would affect NDCG/MRR sensitivity.

Sophie: Can someone try re-eval with a 'preserve-doc-boundaries' mode (no pad-then-slice, strictly slice at doc boundaries) + deterministic candidate sorting? Also run seed 42.

David: Will run that ablation tonight. Also adding a cohort with synthetic negatives vs hard negatives; earlier experiments showed quant gaps sometimes amplify with synthetic negatives.

eval-bot: Eval run 1790001234-1 finished: ndcg@10 -> float32: 0.412, int8: 0.399 (delta -0.013); mrr -> 0.276 -> 0.268. Full report: <gcs://redwood-evals/1790001234-1>

Chen: Thanks for the run. If the preserve-doc-boundaries ablation removes the gap we can blame boundary shifting. If it remains, I’ll dump per-token logits at truncation edges for 5 worst queries and inspect quant rounding behavior.

Priya: +1. Also please ensure candidate sorter is deterministic (tie-break by doc id). Tiny reorders are surprisingly expensive in NDCG tail.

Sophie: Plan: David runs preserve-doc-boundaries + deterministic sorting; Chen dumps logits for failing cases; Priya adds padded-slice ablation and a synthetic-neg cohort. Target: root cause by EOD tomorrow and then decide whether to adjust quant ops or eval harness.

David: Ack — posting results here when complete.

Chen: I'll start the logits dump now and share the slices. If anyone has a quick script to diff token alignments across float32 vs int8, drop it here.

Priya: Dropping my tiny util: `scripts/compare_token_align.py` — pads tokens and prints misaligned suffix/prefix regions. Works with our token ids.

Sophie: Awesome. Thanks all. If this looks like an eval harness issue we should add a regression test to the gauntlet so future quant bring-ups fail fast. :+1:
